questions.prompt: What is the correct signature of the Java program entry point?
questions.explanation: The JVM looks for a public static void main method taking a String array.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a primitive type in Java?
questions.explanation: int is primitive; Integer is its wrapper class, and String and ArrayList are reference types.

questions.prompt: Which keyword is used to make one class inherit from another?
questions.explanation: A class uses extends for class inheritance; implements is for interfaces.

questions.prompt: What is the default value of an int instance field that is not explicitly initialized?
questions.explanation: Numeric fields default to 0; object references default to null.

questions.prompt: Which method should be used to compare the contents of two strings?
questions.explanation: == compares references; equals() compares character content.

questions.prompt: Which collection type does not allow duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: A Set models a mathematical set and rejects duplicates.

questions.prompt: Which keyword prevents a variable from being reassigned after initialization?
questions.explanation: A final variable can be assigned only once. const is reserved but unused in Java.

questions.prompt: What does the expression new String("hi") == new String("hi") evaluate to?
questions.explanation: Each new String creates a distinct object, and == compares references.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a checked exception?
questions.explanation: IOException extends Exception (not RuntimeException), so it must be caught or declared.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a class and interfaces is true?
options: A class can extend multiple classes but implement one interface
A class can neither extend nor implement more than one type
A class can implement multiple interfaces but extend only one class
A class can extend multiple abstract classes
questions.explanation: Java has single class inheritance but allows multiple interface implementation.

questions.prompt: Which statement about HashMap is true?
options: It permits no null keys or values
It keeps entries in insertion order
It permits one null key and multiple null values
questions.explanation: HashMap allows one null key and many null values; it is not synchronized and its ordering is unspecified.

questions.prompt: What does try-with-resources do?
options: Automatically closes resources that implement AutoCloseable when the block exits
Retries the block until it succeeds
Runs the finally block before the try block
questions.explanation: Resources declared in the try header are closed in reverse order, even if an exception occurs.

questions.prompt: What is method overriding?
options: Defining several methods with the same name but different parameters
A subclass providing its own implementation of a method with the same signature
Hiding a field of the superclass
Declaring a method as static in the subclass
questions.explanation: Overriding replaces inherited behavior at runtime; defining same-named methods with different parameters is overloading.

questions.prompt: Which statement about static methods is true?
options: They can directly access instance fields
They can be overridden by subclasses polymorphically
They belong to the class and can be called without creating an instance
They are only callable from within the same object
questions.explanation: Static methods are class-level; they have no this reference and are resolved at compile time.

questions.prompt: In the JVM memory model, where are objects and local primitive variables normally stored?
options: Objects on the stack; local primitives on the heap
Objects on the heap; local primitives on the thread stack
questions.explanation: Each thread has its own stack holding frames with locals; all objects are allocated on the shared heap.

questions.prompt: What does declaring a field volatile guarantee?
options: Visibility of writes across threads and ordering, but not atomicity of compound operations like count++
That the field is stored in thread-local memory
That the field is never garbage collected
questions.explanation: volatile gives happens-before visibility; count++ is still a read-modify-write that needs synchronization or AtomicInteger.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly contrasts ConcurrentHashMap with HashMap?
options: ConcurrentHashMap allows null keys but not null values
ConcurrentHashMap locks the whole map for every operation
ConcurrentHashMap does not allow null keys or values
HashMap is safe for concurrent writes if keys are distinct
questions.explanation: ConcurrentHashMap rejects nulls because null would be ambiguous in concurrent get calls; it uses fine-grained synchronization and CAS.

questions.prompt: What does Integer a = 1000, b = 1000; System.out.println(a == b); print with default JVM settings?
questions.explanation: Autoboxing caches Integer objects only for -128 to 127 by default, so 1000 creates two distinct objects.

questions.prompt: A class overrides equals() but not hashCode(). What problem can occur when instances are used in a HashSet?
options: The HashSet throws an exception on insertion
The equals method is ignored completely
The objects are always rejected as duplicates
Two logically equal objects may land in different buckets, so duplicates or failed lookups occur
questions.explanation: The contract requires equal objects to have equal hash codes; otherwise hash-based collections may not find the equal element.

questions.prompt: When is an object eligible for garbage collection in the HotSpot JVM?
options: When its reference count drops to zero
When System.gc() is called on it
When it is no longer reachable from any GC root, even if objects in a cycle reference each other
questions.explanation: The JVM uses reachability analysis from GC roots, not reference counting, so unreachable cycles are collected.

questions.prompt: What happens if a thread calls obj.wait() without holding obj's monitor?
options: It waits normally and is woken by notify
It blocks forever and cannot be interrupted
questions.explanation: wait, notify and notifyAll must be called from a synchronized block or method on the same object.
